canonical_statement: Time is a parameter or variable necessary to express the dynamical laws of physics.

attributions.surface_quote: time is a parameter or variable necessary to express the dynamical laws of physics.

canonical_statement: In pre-relativistic physics, time was considered a global and universal parameter, independent of external relations or measurements.

attributions.surface_quote: Absolute, true, and mathematical time... passes equably without relation to anything external...

canonical_statement: In relativity, the time variable is defined only within a fixed inertial frame by synchronized stationary clocks.

attributions.surface_quote: In relativity, the time variable “t” is deﬁned only within a ﬁxed inertial frame...

canonical_statement: A natural clock is a device that undergoes a cyclic process according to known physical laws.

attributions.surface_quote: A natural clock is a device undergoing a cyclic process according to known physical laws.

canonical_statement: Time is defined by change according to the dynamical laws of physics.

attributions.surface_quote: time is deﬁned by change according to the dynamical laws of physics

canonical_statement: The simultaneity of distant events is not an absolute concept.

attributions.surface_quote: simultaneity of distant events is not an absolute concept

canonical_statement: Time is defined in a manner that simplifies the description of motion.

attributions.surface_quote: Time is deﬁned so that motion looks simple

canonical_statement: Different inertial frames of reference may experience different time variables.

attributions.surface_quote: we do not need to assume that t = t′

canonical_statement: The synchronization of clocks is relative to the observer's frame of reference.

attributions.surface_quote: clocks of S ′ are seen from the perspective of S, they will not appear synchronized

canonical_statement: Objective reality is constituted by the totality of spacetime events.

attributions.surface_quote: objective reality is comprised of the set of all spacetime “events” that constitute the spacetime manifold.

canonical_statement: An event is defined by its spacetime coordinates (time and position).

attributions.surface_quote: an event E is determined by its spacetime coordinates (t, x), i.e., the when and where it takes place.

canonical_statement: The time variable alone is insufficient to specify objective reality; only the combination of time and space (an event) suffices.

attributions.surface_quote: the time variable alone... is insufficient to specify objective reality, only the pair (t, x) determining an event does.

canonical_statement: The simultaneity of distant events is relative to the observer's inertial frame.

attributions.surface_quote: when in a given inertial frame S... t1 = t2 when x1 ≠ x2, it does not imply that in another inertial frame S′ we must also have t′1 = t′2.

canonical_statement: Objective reality is composed of individual events, not a holistic structure.

attributions.surface_quote: is not part of objective reality, only the individual events are.

canonical_statement: Rational thought and empirical facts are more reliable than naive intuition for understanding reality.

attributions.surface_quote: rely on rational thinking and empirical facts rather than naive everyday intuition.

canonical_statement: The perception of a moving clock lagging is relative to the observer's frame of reference, and this relativity does not imply a logical contradiction.

attributions.surface_quote: the moving clock B is lagging, while an observer fixed with B claims that it is the moving clock A that is lagging without implying any contradiction.

canonical_statement: The absence of contradiction in relative observations of time is due to the comparison of different events and clocks.

attributions.surface_quote: there is no contradiction because different clocks involving different events are being compared in each case.

canonical_statement: The concept of distant simultaneity is not absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: To justify Dingle’s solution one has to assume the absolute character of distant simultaneity.

canonical_statement: Absolute simultaneity is incompatible with the Lorentz transformation.

attributions.surface_quote: absolute simultaneity, which is incompatible with the Lorentz transformation.

canonical_statement: The concept of absolute simultaneity implies the rejection of the principle of light speed invariance.

attributions.surface_quote: Absolute simultaneity implies the rejection of the light principle

canonical_statement: The abandonment of absolute simultaneity is a consequence of excluding the possibility of action at a distance.

attributions.surface_quote: abandonment of absolute simultaneity is a consequence of excluding the possibility of action at a distance

canonical_statement: Instantaneous distant happenings are excluded from objective reality.

attributions.surface_quote: excludes instantaneous distant happenings from objective reality.

canonical_statement: Human intuition can be a misleading guide for understanding objective reality.

attributions.surface_quote: rely on rational thinking and empirical evidence rather than naive human intuition.
